summary_en: This early-phase study tests different doses of tamoxifen in patients with metastatic ER-positive breast cancer that has an ESR1 gene mutation. Tamoxifen is taken by mouth once daily at one of four dose levels (20, 80, 160, or 200 mg), with three participants per level, and is started within 14 days of a FES PET/CT scan and continued until progression or drug intolerance. The study uses FES PET/CT imaging to measure estrogen receptor blockade and find the optimal tamoxifen dose; the record does not state a separate primary outcome measure.
summary_es: Este estudio en fase temprana prueba diferentes dosis de tamoxifeno en pacientes con cáncer de mama metastásico positivo para receptores de estrógeno que tienen una mutación en el gen ESR1. El tamoxifeno se toma por vía oral una vez al día en uno de cuatro niveles de dosis (20, 80, 160 o 200 mg), con tres participantes por nivel, y se inicia dentro de los 14 días posteriores a una tomografía FES PET/CT y se continúa hasta la progresión o la intolerancia al medicamento. El estudio usa la imagen FES PET/CT para medir el bloqueo de los receptores de estrógeno y encontrar la dosis óptima de tamoxifeno; el registro no indica una medida de resultado principal por separado.
who_for: Metastatic or unresectable breast cancer that is ER-positive (10% or more) and HER2 negative.
ESR1 mutation found by a CLIA-certified test on tumor biopsy tissue or circulating free DNA.
Measurable disease per RECIST 1.1, or evaluable bone disease with a lesion of at least 10 mm.
Prior endocrine therapy in the metastatic setting, or progression within 12 months of adjuvant endocrine therapy.
ECOG performance status 0-1, life expectancy over 12 weeks, and ability to take oral medications.
not_for: Tamoxifen, fulvestrant, or other ER-blocking therapy within 60 days before FES PET/CT.
Peripheral neuropathy above grade 1, or significant eye or retinal disorders above grade 1.
History of venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, or stroke.
QTcF of 470 msec or higher, or use of strong CYP2D6, CYP3A4, or CYP2C9 inhibitors or inducers.
